# 2.4 - Normal Distributions and the Empirical Rule {.unnumbered}

Measure the heights of thousands of adult women. Most are close to 64 inches. Fewer are very short or very tall. The histogram makes a smooth **bell shape**.

![](/images/Unit_2/2.4_heights.svg){width="500px" fig-align="center"}

Data with this shape has a {{< glink "normal distribution" >}}. In this lesson, you use one simple rule to find percents in any normal distribution.

:::{.objectives}
- [ ] I describe a normal distribution.
- [ ] I use the empirical rule (68-95-99.7) to find percents.
- [ ] I find the percentile of a value 1, 2, or 3 SDs from the mean.
- [ ] I compare normal curves with different means and SDs.
:::

### 2.4.1 - Normal Distributions

:::{.remember title="A Normal Distribution"}
- is bell-shaped and symmetric
- has the mean and the median in the center (they are equal)
- is described by two numbers: the **mean** $\mu$ (center) and the **SD** $\sigma$ (spread)
:::

A larger SD makes the curve wider and flatter. A different mean moves the curve left or right.

***

### 2.4.2 - The Empirical Rule

![](/images/Unit_2/2.4_empirical.svg){width="620px" fig-align="center"}

:::{.remember title="The 68-95-99.7 Rule"}
- About **68%** of the data is within **1 SD** of the mean, from $\mu - \sigma$ to $\mu + \sigma$.
- About **95%** of the data is within **2 SDs** of the mean, from $\mu - 2\sigma$ to $\mu + 2\sigma$.
- About **99.7%** of the data is within **3 SDs** of the mean, from $\mu - 3\sigma$ to $\mu + 3\sigma$.
:::

**Example:** Heights of adult women have a mean of about 64 inches and an SD of about 3 inches.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Percent from 61 to 67 inches | 68% (within 1 SD) |
| Percent from 58 to 70 inches | 95% (within 2 SDs) |
| Percent taller than 67 inches | $13.5\% + 2.35\% + 0.15\% = 16\%$ |
| Percentile of 67 inches | $100\% - 16\% = 84\%$, the 84th percentile |

:::{.gotcha title="Draw it first"}
Draw the curve and label the mean and the SDs every time. Then shade the part the question asks about and add up the pieces.
:::

:::{.you-try title="Heights again (mean 64, SD 3). What percent of women are shorter than 58 inches?"}
58 is 2 SDs below the mean. The parts below it are $2.35\% + 0.15\% = 2.5\%$.
:::

{{< practice >}}

Work with a partner. Compare answers when you finish each problem.

**Using the Empirical Rule**

1. The weights of apples from one orchard have a normal distribution. The mean is 150 grams and the SD is 10 grams. Draw the curve and label it with the weights. About what percent of the apples weigh:

   a. from 140 to 160 grams?

   b. from 130 to 170 grams?

   c. more than 160 grams?

   d. less than 130 grams?

   e. from 150 to 170 grams?

   f. from 130 to 160 grams?

2. A phone battery lasts a mean of 20 hours with an SD of 2 hours. The times have a normal distribution.

   a. Between what two times do the middle 95% of batteries last?

   b. What percentile is 22 hours?

   c. About what percent of batteries last less than 16 hours?

   d. A battery lasts 27 hours. Is that unusual? Explain.

3. In a normal distribution, what percentile is a value with each z-score?

   a. $z = 0$

   b. $z = 1$

   c. $z = -2$

   d. $z = 2$

   a. The heights of all adult men in Missouri.

   b. The yearly income of every household in the US.
